newsitem.title: USA: U.S. issues warrant for alleged Mexican drug lord.
newsitem.headline: U.S. issues warrant for alleged Mexican drug lord.

text.p: A U.S. arrest warrant was issued for alleged Gulf drug cartel leader Oscar Malherbe de Leon after his capture last month in Mexico, according to recently filed court documents.

The issuance of the warrant came on the same day, March 12, that a U.S. grand jury handed up a new indictment against Malherbe, and may indicate that prosecutors are laying the groundwork to extradite him for trial here.

A spokesman for the Mexican government said on Monday there had been "no formal extradition request" from the United States, but would not comment further. Mexico traditionally has resisted extraditing its citizens.

Malherbe was captured on Feb. 26 in Mexico City and is imprisoned there. He was allegedly a top lieutenant of the Gulf cartel who replaced Juan Garcia Abrego as its leader when Garcia Abrego was captured in the city of Monterrey in January 1996.

Garcia Abrego was shipped to Houston for prosecution on grounds that he was a U.S. citizen. The procedure was described as an "expulsion," not an extradition. He was convicted on multiple drug-trafficking charges in October and sentenced to life in prison without parole.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Melissa Annis told Reuters there was nothing to suggest that Malherbe was a U.S. citizen, but would not comment when asked if the United States had asked Mexico to extradite him.

U.S. officials made it clear earlier this month that they planned to push Mexico to extradite Malherbe and viewed the case as a test of how fully the Mexican government will cooperate in the drug war.
The issue comes at a time when President Bill Clinton is lobbying Congress to support his recent decision to "certify" Mexico's anti-drug efforts as adequate.

The new indictment against Malherbe supersedes an earlier one and appears to play up his role in the Gulf cartel, which prosecutors say shipped thousands of pounds of cocaine to the United States from its base in northern Mexico. It says he became number two in the organisation after the June 1993 arrest of the previous second-in-command, Luis Garcia Medrano.
"Malherbe occupied a position of administrator, organiser and leader within this massive organisation," says the indictment, which charges him with drug trafficking and a number of related offences.
